The instant application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed on behalf of the petitioner seeking regular bail in FIR bearing No. 422/2019, registered at Police Station Mundka, West District, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 363/376 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
2.

The brief facts of the present case are that on the complaint of Mr. Amarjeet (father of victim)
present FIR bearing No. 422/2019, was registered wherein it has been stated by the complainant that his daughter i.e., victim was kidnapped by some unknown person. During the course of investigation on 12.12.2019, kidnapped girl namely, Ms. "A" was produced at the police station by her parents.
After that, the victim got medically examined at SGM Hospital Mangolpuri, Delhi but victim refused for her Gynae examination.
Further on 13.12.2019, the parents of victim came to police station and requested for her medical re-examination.
Accordingly, she was again medically examined at SGM Hospital Mangolpuri, Delhi.

During investigation, statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. of the victim was recorded in which the victim levelled the allegations of kidnapping and Amit Yadav vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60070876/
1 sexual assault on the accused thereafter, Sections 376 IPC and 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO) were added in the present case.

sentences.text: On 07.02.2020, non-bailable warrants were issued by learned POCSO Court, consequently raid was conducted at the address of accused, but the accused was absconding.

During investigation the age proof of victim Ms. 'A' was obtained from her school records and date of birth found to be 30.07.2007 and victim was to be found to be minor (12 years old) at the time of incident.
On 28.09.2020, accused had filed his surrender application before the learned POCSO Court.
During the investigation accused was arrested in the present case and two days police custody remand was taken for further investigation.
After that, the accused was taken for examination at SGM Hospital Mangolpuri, Delhi.
The accused was present before the learned court on 30.09.2020 and was sent to judicial custody.
After the completion of investigation ,chargesheet against the petitioner had already been filed on 14.10.2020.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant states that the applicant in this case has been falsely implicated and the main witnesses in this case have been examined.

It is also stated that the applicant herein was unmarried and was 22 years of age at the time of incident, therefore, bail be granted to the present applicant.
4.

Per contra, learned APP for the State submits that prosecutrix in this case has been examined and the prosecutrix has supported the case of prosecution and therefore, bail be rejected since chances of conviction are higher in this case and other witnesses remain to be examined.

5. Keeping in view all the facts and circumstances of the case and having considered that the prosecutrix has been examined in this case and the accused has remained in judicial custody for more than 2  years, investigation stands completed and charge-sheet has been filed.

6. Thus, this Court is inclined to grant regular bail to the petitioner on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned on the following terms and conditions:
i. The applicant shall remain available on mobile numbers; shared by him with the Police.
ii. The applicant shall not leave NCT of Delhi without prior permission of the concerned court.
iii. The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make an attempt to influence the witnesses or tamper with the evidence in any manner.
iv. In case of change of residential address/contact details, the applicant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Court.
7. Accordingly, the present bail application stands disposed of.
8. The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
